slides.title: Development
slides.speaker_notes: What does it mean to be developed?

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Use per capita income to compare countries.
List 3 limits of using income alone.
Describe the role of public facilities.
Use IMR / literacy / life expectancy to compare states.

slides.title: Development means different things
bullets: Goals can even CONFLICT (dam vs displaced family).
Mix of MATERIAL and NON-MATERIAL needs.
Even the rich want non-material things.

slides.title: What does each person want?
bullets: Landless labourer — more days of work + higher wage.
Punjab farmer — better minimum prices + reliable electricity.
Working woman — safe workplace + skills + loans.
Urban youth — a job that lasts.

slides.title: Comparing countries — per capita income
bullets: World Bank groups: HIGH / MIDDLE / LOW.
India is in LOW-MIDDLE income group.

slides.title: Limits of per capita income
bullets: Hides INEQUALITY — same average ≠ same lives.
Public goods cannot be bought individually.

slides.title: Public facilities
bullets: Rich can sometimes buy private alternatives.
Raise quality of life for everyone.

slides.title: Indicators beyond income
bullets: IMR — children dying per 1000 live births.
Use them TOGETHER for a fuller picture.

slides.title: Kerala vs Haryana — the puzzle
bullets: Why? Kerala invested more in public health + education.

slides.title: Human Development Index (HDI)
bullets: Combines: per capita income + life expectancy + schooling.
Sri Lanka has higher HDI than India.

slides.title: Sustainability — Brundtland
bullets: Meet PRESENT needs without compromising the future.

slides.title: Three sustainability examples
bullets: GROUNDWATER — India largest extractor; wells drying.
CRUDE OIL — only 35–40 years left at current rates.
FORESTS — cutting reduces rain, biodiversity, soil.

slides.title: You try (5 min)
bullets: 2. Three limits of income as a measure.
3. Why does Kerala have lower IMR than Haryana?
5. One groundwater concern in your state.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. World Bank groups countries on?
Q3. Best development indicator: IMR or PCI?

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Development is plural — material + non-material goals.
Per capita income compares countries; World Bank: high / middle / low.
Income alone hides inequality and ignores public goods.
Public facilities matter most for the poor.
IMR / literacy / NAR / life expectancy complete the picture.
Sustainability is essential — groundwater, oil, forests, climate.
